latestTerminalSummary:
Target T is still open. The count stays **4/10**. The new result is a necessary photon-rate comparison at equality, and it does not force the inputs to be Gaussian.

The report is `frontier/campaigns/2026-10-14/epni-gaussianity-r2/candidate.md`. Round 1 was not modified. Its candidate digest is still `8c227f21c39e205f8cf95d58f03d82bb06ed7a4e63cdbbe04336d82a8b88353d`.

**Theorem R.** At an entropy photon-number equality, for every positive-definite noise covariance \(\gamma\), the output’s entropy-photon difference quotients dominate each input’s: the liminf on \(C\) is at least the limsup on \(A\), and the same holds for \(B\). When an input has positive entropy, the photon rates exist in \([0,\infty]\) and \(\kappa_\gamma(C)\ge\kappa_\gamma(A)\), \(\kappa_\gamma(C)\ge\kappa_\gamma(B)\). Every Gaussian pair in Target T saturates this, including unequal entropy and a pure input. For shape-matched noise \(G=SS^T\) the common rate is \(1\).

That necessary condition is compatible with the whole extremal family, so it does not pay the unequal-entropy Gaussianity step. Varying the two noise speeds gives nothing beyond the same maximum. The convex combination \(\kappa(C)\le\eta\kappa(A)+(1-\eta)\kappa(B)\) is false for the physical one-mode pair \(\operatorname{diag}(5,1)\) and \(\operatorname{diag}(1,3/5)\) at \(\eta=1/2\): the gap is \(\sqrt5(11\sqrt3-18)/60\), and \(363>324\). That pair is itself a strict inequality, since \(27>25\). The one-mode isotropic maximum bound is true and still too weak to equalize the two inputs. Harmonic saturation of isotropic Fisher information fails on the unequal thermal extremizers, which do saturate the photon-rate bound, because \(w=1/h\) is strictly concave. Isotropic noise on a common squeeze leaves the equality set at second order: for \(s=2\), \(a=1/10\), \(b=1\), \(\eta=1/2\), the deficit has \(\delta'(0)=0\) and \(\delta''(0)=675/896\).

The seven round-1 obstructions are kept. No counterexample to Target T is claimed. `checks/verify_manifest.py` reproduced the rational checks and the owned inventory: 8 inputs, 8 output records, 5 pinned sections. This is not an independent review and not a Lean certificate.
